front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its Residential Care Facility for the Elderly (RCFE) in California. It turns the requirements of the California licensing regulations (Title 22, California Code of Regulations), the related Health and Safety Code and Welfare and Institutions Code provisions, and other applicable rules into written, day-to-day procedures that staff can follow.

The manual is intended to:

- Protect the health, safety, dignity and personal rights of every resident of **[AGENCY NAME]**.
- Give administrators, direct care staff, and other personnel one consistent reference for admission, care, medication assistance, staffing, training, emergency response, reporting, and recordkeeping.
- Support the facility's Plan of Operation and show licensing staff, residents, families and representatives how the facility meets its obligations.
- Make sure required reports, notices, and records are made on time and kept for the required period.

**This manual is a template and must be customized.** Every [AGENCY NAME] placeholder, and every other bracketed field (for example [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], [LICENSED CAPACITY], [GOVERNING BODY], [ADOPTION DATE], [LOCAL FIRE AUTHORITY]), must be replaced with facility-specific information. Policies must also be adjusted to match your licensed capacity, resident population, services offered (for example dementia care, hospice, or Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver participation), and your approved Plan of Operation. Delete or revise any section that does not apply to your facility.

This manual is an operational guide. It is not legal advice and does not replace the regulations themselves. If this manual and a statute or regulation ever differ, the statute or regulation controls.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

### 1. Customize before use
- Replace all **[AGENCY NAME]** and other bracketed placeholders with your facility's information.
- Confirm each policy against your licensed capacity, your approved Plan of Operation, and the services you actually provide.
- Where a policy depends on facility size (for example night supervision, or medication assistance training hours for homes of 15 or fewer versus 16 or more), keep the version that applies to you and remove the other.
- Enter the real names and phone numbers for your administrator, designated substitute, Infection Control Lead, local fire authority, local ombudsman, and local health officer.

### 2. Adopt formally
- The completed manual must be reviewed and **adopted by [GOVERNING BODY]** (the owner, board of directors, or other governing authority of [AGENCY NAME]).
- Record the adoption in the minutes or another written record. Enter the **[ADOPTION DATE]** and **[VERSION NUMBER]** on the cover page.
- Have each later revision adopted the same way.

### 3. Keep it current
- Assign a responsible person, **[NAME/TITLE]**, to review the manual at least annually and whenever a regulation, a licensing instruction, your Plan of Operation, or your services change.
- Review the infection control sections (see 22 CCR §87470) at the times that regulation requires.
- Check the linked sources in the Regulatory Framework section against the current published text before relying on any summary here. Summaries in this manual are shortened and may be outdated by later amendments.
- Keep a revision log, and retire superseded copies.

### 4. Train staff on it
- Every employee, and every volunteer where applicable, must be trained on the policies relevant to their role **before** they perform those duties, and again whenever a policy changes.
- Give staff access to the manual, and keep it readily available at the facility. Some items, such as the emergency disaster plan, must be written and readily available (see 22 CCR §87212).
- Document each training: date, topics, trainer, and attendees. Keep the records in personnel files as the regulations require.
- This manual's orientation does not replace the training required by law (for example under HSC §§1569.625, 1569.626, and 1569.69, and 22 CCR §87411). It supplements that training.

### 5. Everyday use
- Use the table of contents and the cite references in each policy to find the governing rule.
- Follow posted and written procedures for emergencies, reporting, and medication assistance. Deadlines for reports are short, and several run from the time of the incident.
- When a situation is not covered, or a rule seems unclear, ask the administrator or designated substitute. If still unclear, contact the licensing agency (see Regulators below) or qualified legal counsel.
- Do not use this manual to justify an action that conflicts with a resident's personal rights or with the law.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

The policies in this manual are drawn from the following rules. Cites are listed exactly as they appear in the source list for this manual. Each summary is brief. **Always consult the linked source for the full, current text.**

### Licensing, Plan of Operation, and Business Requirements
- **22 CCR §87208**: Plan of Operation. Written plan covering purposes and goals, admission agreement and policies, administrative organization, staffing and training plan, dimensioned sketches, transportation, handling of resident money, visiting policy, approach to resident behavioral expression, and the infection control plan.
- **22 CCR §87202**: Fire Clearance. Required before licensure; a separate clearance is required before accepting or keeping nonambulatory or bedridden residents.
- **HSC §1569.185**: License fees. Annual fee due each license anniversary (with late fee), and a fee for capacity changes.
- **HSC §1569.605**: Liability insurance minimums ($1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate for injury to residents and guests caused by negligence).
- **LIC 281 (Application Instructions for a Facility License), Sections A and B**: Application attachments, including the written theft and loss policy (B14), neighborhood complaint policy where applicable (B15), sample menu (B10), and job descriptions and personnel policies (B4–B5).

### Admission, Appraisal, and Resident Rights
- **22 CCR §87457**: Pre-Admission Appraisal. Pre-admission interview and functional, mental and social evaluation, with consent and a suitability determination before admission.
- **22 CCR §87507**: Admission Agreements. Individual written agreement in plain language, signed and dated within 7 days of admission, covering services, rates, notices, refunds, visiting and firearms policies, grievance procedure, eviction grounds, and the right to contact CDSS and the ombudsman; no liability-waiver provisions.
- **22 CCR §87615**: Prohibited Health Conditions. Conditions for which residents cannot be admitted or retained (the list is not exhaustive).
- **22 CCR §87468.1**: Personal Rights of Residents in all Facilities. Eighteen personal rights, including protections against discrimination based on actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, or HIV status. The Department cannot waive those protections.
- **22 CCR §87217**: Safeguards for Resident Cash, Personal Property, and Valuables. Receipts, accounting records, and a separate account for residents' money if the facility holds it; no commingling.
- **42 CFR §441.301(c)**: HCBS Settings Rule. Applies **only if** the facility enrolls in the Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver.

### Dementia, Hospice, and Special Services
- **22 CCR §87705**: Care of Persons with Dementia. Awake night supervision in homes with fewer than 16 beds when a resident with dementia needs it.
- **22 CCR §87706**: Advertising Dementia Special Care. A written dementia program is required for facilities that advertise dementia care; advertisements must be kept for 3 years.
- **22 CCR §87632**: Hospice Care Waiver. Written request stating the maximum number of hospice residents; CDSS decides within 30 days of an acceptable request.

### Resident Care, Medications, and Infection Control
- **22 CCR §87465**: Incidental Medical and Dental Care Services. Plan for incidental care; limits on medication assistance; PRN order requirements; storage, destruction, and record retention; first aid kit and posted emergency numbers.
- **22 CCR §87470**: Infection Control Requirements. Written infection control plan (LIC 9282), a trained Infection Control Lead, staff training, and required reviews.

### Administrator, Staffing, and Training
- **22 CCR §87405**: Administrator-Qualifications and Duties.
- **HSC §1569.616**: Administrator certification (initial certification program and exam, and continuing education).
- **22 CCR §87411**: Personnel Requirements-General. Staffing sufficiency, age, training, health screening, criminal record clearance, and limits on residents and volunteers filling required staff roles.
- **22 CCR §87355**: Criminal Record Clearance.
- **22 CCR §87415**: Night Supervision (RCFE).
- **HSC §1569.625**: Direct care staff training (initial and annual hours).
- **HSC §1569.626**: Dementia training for direct care staff.
- **HSC §1569.69**: Medication assistance training.
- **Labor Code §246**: Paid sick leave.
- **IWC Wage Order 5**: Meal and rest rules for 24-hour residential care of the elderly. Live-in and 24-hour shifts need employment counsel.

### Physical Plant, Maintenance, and Emergency Preparedness
- **22 CCR §87212**: Emergency Disaster Plan. Written, readily available disaster and mass casualty plan; emergency exit plans and telephone numbers must be posted.
- **22 CCR §87307**: Personal Accommodations and Services (bedroom occupancy and toilet, washbasin, and bathing fixture ratios).
- **22 CCR §87303**: Maintenance and Operation (heat, hot water, plant maintenance, and private water supply testing).

### Incident and Abuse Reporting
- **22 CCR §87211**: Reporting Requirements. Time-limited reports to the licensing agency, local health officer, fire authority, ombudsman, and law enforcement; notices of financial and corporate changes; notices of a new administrator.
- **W&I Code §15630**: Elder and dependent adult abuse mandated reporting. Facility staff are mandated reporters. The facility-specific 2-hour and 24-hour timeframes are restated in 22 CCR §87211(b),(c).

citations.title: Personal Rights of Residents in all Facilities
citations.requirement: Lists 18 personal rights: dignity; freedom from punishment, humiliation, intimidation or abuse; being told how to complain to CCLD and the ombudsman; leaving at any time and not being locked in; private visits by ombudsmen and advocates at reasonable hours without prior notice; keeping and spending own money; phone, mail, voting and refusing care; moving out. Subsection (b) bars denial of admission, transfer, discharge, room sharing, room or restroom assignment, preferred name or pronouns, and association, based on actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status. Subsection (d): the Department cannot waive the (b) protections.

citations.title: Emergency Disaster Plan
citations.requirement: A written, readily available disaster and mass casualty plan. It must cover: administrative authority and staff assignments; fire safety plan; means of exiting; assembly at a predetermined evacuation site; transportation; relocation sites equipped for safe temporary accommodation; supervision during evacuation and contact after relocation; contact with fire, law enforcement and disaster agencies; and notifying a resident's hospice agency on evacuation or relocation. Emergency exit plans and telephone numbers must be posted.

citations.title: Personnel Requirements-General
citations.requirement: Personnel must be sufficient in numbers and competent. CDSS may require more staff when documentation shows a need. Anyone supervising staff or residents must be 18 or older. Staff assisting with personal ADLs get initial and annual training under HSC §§1569.625 and 1569.69, plus first aid from a qualified provider. Required training topics are listed, with trainer qualifications and documentation in personnel records. All personnel need a physician health screening (chest x-ray or intradermal test) within 6 months before or 7 days after employment. Criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer is required before employment or presence. Residents cannot substitute for required staff. Volunteers must be supervised and are not counted in the staffing plan.

citations.title: Incidental Medical and Dental Care Services
citations.requirement: Requires a plan for incidental medical and dental care. Staff may only assist with self-administered medications and may not give injections unless authorized by law. Assistance cannot include forcing, hiding or camouflaging medications. PRN rules: a signed, dated physician order on a prescription blank, with symptoms, exact dose, minimum hours between doses and maximum doses per 24 hours. Central storage in a locked place, in the original container, with a record kept at least 1 year. Destruction by the administrator and one other non-resident adult, with a record kept at least 3 years. First aid kit; emergency numbers posted; ambulance number available; call 9-1-1 for an imminent threat to health.

citations.title: Admission Agreements
citations.requirement: Individual written agreement in 12-point type, plain language, with titled sections. Signed and dated within 7 days of admission. Copy given immediately, and a copy or notice of availability posted. Must specify basic services, additional services, rates, payment, 60 days' written notice of rate changes, refund conditions, preadmission fee limits and refunds, visiting policy, firearms policy, grievance procedure, eviction grounds and notice rights, and the right to contact CDSS and the ombudsman. LIC 9158 is required when the appraisal shows a hearing or other disability. No liability-waiver provisions.

citations.title: Prohibited Health Conditions
citations.requirement: Residents who need health services for, or have, these conditions cannot be admitted or retained: stage 3 and 4 pressure injuries, gastrostomy tubes, naso-gastric tubes, staph or other serious infection, total dependence on others for all ADLs, and tracheostomies. The list is not exhaustive ("including, but not limited to").

citations.title: Reporting Requirements
citations.requirement: (a)(1) Written report to the licensing agency and the person responsible for the resident within 7 days of any death, any serious injury as determined by the physician, any AED use, or any incident threatening welfare, safety or health (including unexplained absence or psychological abuse). (a)(2) Outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes and major accidents: within 24 hours by phone or fax to the licensing agency and the local health officer. (a)(3) Fires and explosions: immediately to the local fire authority, and no later than the next working day to the licensing agency. (b),(c) Suspected physical abuse of an elder or dependent adult: report to the local ombudsman, licensing agency and local law enforcement within 2 hours if serious bodily injury, otherwise within 24 hours. (d),(e),(f) Written notice within 2 business days of foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default notice or utility shut-off notice; notice to applicants before signing; civil penalty of $100 per day, up to $2,000. (g) Notice of a new administrator within 30 days. (h) Change of chief corporate officer within 15 working days.

citations.title: Night Supervision (RCFE)
citations.requirement: Fewer than 16 residents: a qualified person on call on the premises overnight. 16–100 residents: one employee awake on duty plus one on call within 10 minutes. Night staff must know the emergency plan and be first-aid trained. (Per fact-checked research S7.)

citations.title: Care of Persons with Dementia
citations.requirement: In homes with fewer than 16 beds, at least one night staff person must be awake and on duty when a resident with dementia needs awake night supervision, based on appraisal, reappraisal or observation. (Per fact-checked research S8.)

citations.title: Advertising Dementia Special Care
citations.requirement: A facility that advertises dementia care must have a written dementia program covering philosophy, admission, training, activities, environment, changes in condition and success indicators. Keep advertisements for 3 years. (Per fact-checked research S27 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Plan of Operation
citations.requirement: Written plan covering purposes and goals, admission agreement, admission policies, administrative organization, staffing and training plan, dimensioned sketches, transportation, handling of resident money, visiting policy, approach to resident behavioral expression, and the infection control plan. (Per fact-checked research S23.)

citations.title: Fire Clearance
citations.requirement: Fire clearance is required before licensure. A separate fire clearance is required before accepting or keeping nonambulatory or bedridden residents. (Per fact-checked research S28.)

citations.title: Personal Accommodations and Services
citations.requirement: No more than 2 residents per bedroom; at least 1 toilet and washbasin per 6 persons and 1 tub or shower per 10, counting live-in staff and family. (Per fact-checked research S24.)

citations.title: Maintenance and Operation
citations.requirement: Heat of at least 68°F; hot water 105–120°F; plant maintenance standards; private water supply testing (annually for capacity 7–15). (Per fact-checked research S69 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Criminal Record Clearance
citations.requirement: DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance or exemption is required for the applicant, administrator, adult household members and staff before they work or are present. (Per fact-checked research S29.)

citations.title: Safeguards for Resident Cash, Personal Property, and Valuables
citations.requirement: If the facility holds resident cash, it must keep receipts and accounting records and a separate account titled as the residents' money, with no commingling. LIC 400 affidavit and LIC 402 surety bond. (Per fact-checked research S70.)

citations.title: Administrator-Qualifications and Duties
citations.requirement: Administrator must be 21 or older with a high school diploma or equivalent and good character, and must be certified. Added education and experience for 16+ beds. Must be on premises a sufficient number of hours, with a designated qualified substitute when absent. (Per fact-checked research S14.)

citations.title: Infection Control Requirements
citations.requirement: Written infection control plan (LIC 9282). Name an Infection Control Lead trained by a qualified professional. Set initial and ongoing staff training. Review annually, after an outbreak declaration, or at the licensing agency's request. (Per fact-checked research S32.)

citations.title: Hospice Care Waiver
citations.requirement: Written request stating the maximum number of hospice residents; CDSS decides within 30 days of an acceptable request. (Per fact-checked research S26.)

citations.title: Pre-Admission Appraisal
citations.requirement: Pre-admission interview and functional, mental and social evaluation, with consent and a suitability determination against admission criteria before admission. (Per fact-checked research S35 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Administrator certification
citations.requirement: 80-hour initial certification program (at least 60 hours live) and state exam within 60 days. 40 hours of CE every 2 years, including 8 hours on dementia. (Per fact-checked research S13.)

citations.title: Direct care staff training
citations.requirement: 40 hours initial: 20 before working alone and 20 within 4 weeks. The first 20 include 6 hours dementia and 4 hours postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice. 20 hours annually, including 8 hours dementia. (Per fact-checked research S10.)

citations.title: Dementia training for direct care staff
citations.requirement: Dementia training for direct care staff: 12 hours initial and 8 hours annually. (Per fact-checked research S11.)

citations.title: Medication assistance training
citations.requirement: Homes of 15 or fewer: 10 hours initial (6 hands-on before assisting, 4 within 2 weeks) plus an exam; 8 hours annually. Homes of 16+: 24 hours initial (16 hands-on, 8 within 4 weeks) plus an exam; 8 hours annually. (Per fact-checked research S12.)

citations.title: Elder and dependent adult abuse mandated reporting
citations.requirement: Care custodians and facility staff are mandated reporters. Report by phone immediately or as soon as practicably possible, then in writing within the statutory time (SOC 341). The facility-specific 2-hour and 24-hour timeframes are restated in 22 CCR §87211(b),(c). (Per fact-checked research S36.)

citations.title: Liability insurance minimums
citations.requirement: Liability insurance of $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate for injury to residents and guests caused by negligence. (Per fact-checked research S18.)

citations.title: HCBS Settings Rule (applies to Assisted Living Waiver settings)
citations.requirement: HCBS settings must include a lease or agreement, privacy, resident choice, and access to food and visitors. Applies only if the RCFE enrolls in the Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver. (Per fact-checked research.)

citations.title: License fees
citations.requirement: Annual fee of $495.60 (4–6 beds) or $742.80 (7–15 beds), due each license anniversary, with a 50% late fee. Capacity change fee of $25. (Per fact-checked research S1.)

citations.title: Paid sick leave
citations.requirement: At least 40 hours or 5 days of paid sick leave per year. (Per fact-checked research S57.)

citations.title: Meal and rest rules for 24-hour residential care of the elderly
citations.requirement: Special meal and rest period rules for a sole caregiver in 24-hour residential care for the elderly. Live-in and 24-hour shifts need employment counsel. (Per fact-checked research S60.)

citations.cite: LIC 281 (Application Instructions for a Facility License), Sections A and B
citations.title: Application attachments (theft and loss policy B14; neighborhood complaint policy B15; sample menu B10; job descriptions B4–B5)
citations.requirement: Written theft and loss policy (B14); neighborhood complaint policy when the owner does not live in a home serving 6 or fewer (B15); sample menu (B10); job descriptions and personnel policies (B4–B5). (Per fact-checked research S21.)

policies.title: Licensee Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Licensee, governing body, certified administrator, designated substitute administrator
policies.purpose: To define who is accountable for the operation of [AGENCY NAME], what the certified administrator must do, and how changes in administration or corporate leadership are reported to the California Department of Social Services (CDSS).
policies.policy: The licensee's governing body is accountable for the operation of the Residential Care Facility for the Elderly (RCFE) and for compliance with Title 22 and the RCFE Act. The governing body appoints a certified administrator who meets 22 CCR §87405 and who is on the premises a sufficient number of hours to run the facility. When the administrator is absent, a qualified substitute is designated in writing. Residents and volunteers are never counted as staff. The governing body gives CDSS timely written notice of any change of administrator or chief corporate officer. The administrator carries out the plan of operation (22 CCR §87208) and does not delegate legal accountability.

definitions.definition: The individual, partnership, corporation or other entity to which CDSS issued the RCFE license, and which is legally responsible for the facility.
The owner(s), board of directors or other persons with ultimate authority over [AGENCY NAME].
The person certified under Title 22 and HSC rules who is responsible for day-to-day operation and who meets the qualifications of 22 CCR §87405.
A person named in writing, meeting the qualifications for an administrator or substitute, who has authority and responsibility when the administrator is absent.
The top executive officer of a corporate licensee, whose change must be reported to CDSS.

procedures: The governing body adopts a written resolution or minutes appointing [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] as certified administrator and records the appointment date. The licensee retains the document in the governance file.

Before appointment, the governing body verifies that the administrator is at least 21 years old, holds a high school diploma or equivalent, has good character, and holds a current administrator certificate. A copy of the certificate and supporting records is kept in the administrator's personnel file.
For a facility of 16 or more beds, the governing body also verifies the added education and experience required by 22 CCR §87405 before appointment.

The governing body approves a written weekly schedule showing the hours the administrator is on the premises. Those hours must be sufficient for the size and needs of the facility. The administrator posts the schedule in the office.

The administrator names a qualified substitute on the CDSS designation form (LIC 308). The administrator reviews it at least annually and whenever the substitute changes, and keeps the current LIC 308 on site.

When the administrator is absent, the substitute assumes full responsibility. Before departing, the administrator briefs the substitute on resident changes of condition, pending incidents, and how to reach the administrator at [PHONE].
The administrator implements the plan of operation (22 CCR §87208) and the policies in this manual, and ensures staff are trained to follow them.
The administrator ensures that staffing is sufficient and competent every shift. Residents and volunteers are never counted toward required staffing or used in place of staff.

The administrator reports to the governing body at least quarterly on census, incidents, staffing, complaints, inspection findings and finances. The governing body records its review in meeting minutes.

If the administrator leaves or a new administrator is hired, the licensee notifies CDSS in writing within 30 days. The notice includes the administrator's name, addresses, start date, background and qualifications, and a copy of the administrator certificate.
If the chief corporate officer changes, the licensee notifies CDSS within 15 working days and submits the required fingerprint card for the new officer.

The licensee and administrator keep CDSS Community Care Licensing, Adult and Senior Care Program, (916) 657-2592, as the regulator contact. The administrator responds to licensing evaluator requests and visits promptly and completes any plan of correction by the stated deadline.

If no certified administrator is available, the governing body immediately designates a qualified substitute and takes steps to fill the position. It does not allow the facility to operate without qualified administrative oversight.
The governing body reviews this policy annually and when regulations change.

responsibilities.duty: Appoint and oversee the administrator, ensure legal compliance, make the required notices to CDSS, and review administrator reports quarterly.
Maintain certification, be on the premises for the scheduled hours, run daily operations, maintain the substitute designation and supervise all staff.
Hold full authority and responsibility for operations during the administrator's absence and report incidents on return.
Follow the chain of authority and contact the administrator or substitute for urgent decisions.

documentation: Governing body resolution or minutes appointing the administrator
Administrator certificate and qualification records
Administrator weekly on-premises schedule
Current LIC 308 substitute designation
Written notices to CDSS of administrator and corporate officer changes, with proof of delivery
Quarterly administrator reports and governing body minutes

policies.title: Administrator Certification, Continuing Education and Designated Substitute
policies.applies_to: Administrator, designated substitute, governing body
policies.purpose: To ensure the administrator and any substitute hold and maintain the certification required by California law, so that [AGENCY NAME] is always led by a qualified person.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will be directed only by an administrator who is at least 21 years old, has a high school diploma or equivalent, is of good character, and holds a current RCFE administrator certificate (22 CCR §87405; HSC §1569.616). The administrator completes the initial 80-hour certification program (at least 60 hours live), passes the state exam within 60 days, and completes 40 hours of continuing education (CE) every 2 years, including 8 hours on dementia. A qualified substitute is designated for administrator absences. The facility tracks all deadlines to avoid delinquency fees and lapse.

definitions.definition: An 80-hour CDSS-approved course, at least 60 hours of which must be live, that is a prerequisite for the administrator exam.
40 hours every 2 years from approved vendors, including 8 hours on dementia, with no more than half self-paced.
The CDSS Administrator Certification Bureau, 916-653-9300, AdminCertInfo@dss.ca.gov.
A $300 fee charged when certificate renewal is late.

procedures: Before hiring or designating anyone as administrator, the licensee confirms the person is 21 or older, holds a high school diploma or equivalent, and has references showing good character. The licensee records these checks in the personnel file.

For a candidate without a certificate, the licensee enrolls the candidate in a CDSS-approved 80-hour initial certification program with at least 60 live hours, and keeps the enrollment and completion records.
The candidate submits the certificate application ($140) and the exam fee ($100) to the Administrator Certification Bureau. The licensee tracks the payment receipts.
The candidate takes the state exam within 60 days of completing the course. The administrator calendars the deadline on the day the course ends.
The administrator files a copy of the issued certificate in the personnel file and posts or makes it available as required by CDSS.
The administrator selects CE courses only from CDSS-approved vendors and confirms that the 40 hours over 2 years include 8 hours on dementia and that no more than half are self-paced.
The administrator keeps every CE completion certificate in the personnel file and updates the CE tracking log after each course.

The licensee sets calendar reminders 180, 90 and 30 days before the certificate renewal date. The administrator submits renewal and CE documentation before the deadline to avoid the $300 delinquency fee.

The administrator designates at least one qualified substitute in writing on LIC 308 and verifies that the substitute meets Title 22 qualifications. A copy of the substitute's qualification records is kept on site.
Before the substitute's first period of coverage, the administrator trains the substitute on facility policies, emergency procedures, resident needs, and how to reach the administrator at [PHONE].
If certification lapses or a certificate is revoked, the licensee immediately removes the person from administrator duties, designates a qualified replacement, and notifies CDSS as required.
The governing body reviews the certification and CE log every quarter and the administrator reports any gaps within 5 business days.

For questions about certification, exams or approved vendors, the administrator contacts the Certification Bureau at 916-653-9300 or AdminCertInfo@dss.ca.gov and records the date and outcome of the contact.

responsibilities.duty: Hold a current certificate, complete CE on time, keep records and name a qualified substitute.
Verify qualifications before appointment, fund required training and review the tracking log quarterly.
Maintain qualifications and complete orientation before serving.

documentation: Proof of age, diploma or equivalent, and character references
80-hour course completion certificate
Application and exam fee receipts
Administrator certificate copy
CE tracking log and completion certificates
LIC 308 substitute designation and substitute qualification records
Renewal reminders and renewal confirmation

policies.title: Licensure, Posting and Regulatory Compliance
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, designated substitute
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] holds all required licenses and clearances, pays fees on time, posts required notices, and notifies CDSS of changes.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates only under a current CDSS RCFE license and applicable fire clearance. The administrator keeps the license posted and ensures that required postings, fees and notifications are current. Required postings are the license, a copy of the approved admission agreement (or notice of its availability), emergency exit plans and telephone numbers, emergency agency numbers visible to staff and residents, and the ombudsman CRISISline and local ombudsman number. The facility does not accept nonambulatory or bedridden residents without the separate fire clearance. It does not change licensed capacity or location without first notifying and obtaining approval from CDSS.

definitions.definition: Approval from the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal required before licensure and, separately, before accepting or keeping nonambulatory or bedridden residents (22 CCR §87202).
$495.60 for 4–6 beds or $742.80 for 7–15 beds, due on each license anniversary, with a 50% late penalty (HSC §1569.185).
A $25 fee when licensed capacity is changed.
1-800-231-4024, the California Long-Term Care Ombudsman line.

procedures: The administrator posts the original license in a conspicuous public area, such as the entrance, and checks monthly that it is in place and undamaged.
The administrator posts a complete copy of the approved admission agreement or a notice that a copy is available upon request (22 CCR §87507). The posting is checked monthly.

The administrator posts the emergency exit plans and emergency telephone numbers in locations visible to residents and staff (22 CCR §87212). Numbers include fire, law enforcement, ambulance, poison control and the facility's disaster contacts.
The administrator posts emergency agency numbers where staff and residents can see them, and keeps the ambulance number available (22 CCR §87465).
The administrator posts the ombudsman CRISISline 1-800-231-4024 and the local ombudsman number where residents and visitors can see them.
The administrator confirms that the facility's advertising and any display of the license number follow Title 22 rules, and that the administrator reviews each new advertisement before release.
The administrator calendars the annual license fee for each license anniversary and pays it at least 30 days before it is due. Payment confirmation is filed. Late payment adds a 50% penalty.

Before accepting any nonambulatory or bedridden resident, the administrator confirms that the facility holds the separate fire clearance required by 22 CCR §87202. Without it, the facility does not admit or keep the resident.
Before any change in licensed capacity, the administrator notifies CDSS and submits the $25 capacity change fee. The facility does not exceed licensed capacity.
Before moving locations or making a major structural change, the licensee consults CDSS Community Care Licensing at (916) 657-2592 and does not proceed until CDSS gives written direction.
The administrator completes a monthly posting checklist, initials it and files it. Missing or outdated items are corrected within 24 hours.
The administrator reviews CDSS correspondence, evaluation reports and plans of correction upon receipt, and completes any corrective action by the due date shown.
The administrator files all licensing documents in the licensing binder, available to any CDSS evaluator at any time.

responsibilities.duty: Hold and renew the license, pay fees and approve capacity or location changes.
Maintain all postings, track fees and fire clearance, notify CDSS of changes and respond to regulatory findings.
Make documents available to a licensing evaluator during the administrator's absence.

documentation: Original license and licensing binder
Fire clearance(s), including nonambulatory/bedridden clearance if applicable
Annual license fee payments
Capacity change notices and fee receipts
Monthly posting checklists
CDSS evaluation reports and plans of correction

policies.title: Plan of Operation, Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, all staff
policies.purpose: To keep a current written plan of operation and policy manual that meets California requirements, is available at inspection and is controlled, reviewed and communicated to staff.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written plan of operation as required by 22 CCR §87208, kept on site and kept current. It contains: purposes and goals; the admission agreement; admission policies; administrative organization; the staffing and training plan; dimensioned sketches of the floor plan and grounds (LIC 999); transportation; handling of resident money; the visiting policy; the approach to resident behavioral expression; and the infection control plan. Job descriptions and personnel policies, including an awake night shift duty statement, are maintained as application attachments (LIC 281, B4–B5). The manual is controlled by version and reviewed at least annually.

definitions.definition: The written description of the facility's program and administration required by 22 CCR §87208.
A scaled floor plan and grounds sketch with measurements, submitted on form LIC 999.
The system of version numbers, approval dates and distribution records ensuring staff use only the current policy.
A written description of night staff duties, including supervision, rounds and emergency response.

procedures: The administrator prepares the plan of operation with all required elements: purposes and goals, admission agreement, admission policies, administrative organization, staffing and training plan, dimensioned sketches, transportation, resident money, visiting policy, behavioral expression approach and infection control plan.
The administrator prepares the floor plan and grounds sketch on form LIC 999 with all rooms, exits and dimensions, and updates it after any physical change.
The administrator writes job descriptions and personnel policies for each position (LIC 281, B4–B5) and includes an awake night shift duty statement.
The governing body reviews and approves the plan of operation and signs and dates the approval page. The administrator records the version number and effective date on every policy.
The administrator keeps a complete copy of the manual at the facility in a location accessible to staff and available for the pre-licensing inspection and later CDSS visits.
Each staff member signs an acknowledgment during orientation that they have read the policies relevant to their role. The administrator files the acknowledgment in the personnel record.

The administrator reviews the whole manual at least annually, and sooner after a regulation change, CDSS finding, serious incident or change in services. The review is recorded on the document control log with date and reviewer.

If a change would alter the program in a way that affects licensure, the administrator consults CDSS Community Care Licensing at (916) 657-2592 before implementing it. Requests for flexibility from regulations are submitted to CDSS for written approval and are not implemented before approval.
When a policy is revised, the administrator marks the old version as superseded, removes it from working binders, retains it in the archive and issues the new version to staff within 7 days.
The administrator trains staff on every material policy change and records attendance with date, topic and trainer.
The administrator confirms that residents or their representatives can request the visiting policy, the admission agreement and the grievance procedure.
The administrator audits the manual annually against the checklist of required plan of operation elements. Gaps are corrected within 30 days.

responsibilities.duty: Approve the plan of operation and any material revisions.
Draft, maintain and distribute the plan and policies, run annual review and train staff.
Read, acknowledge and follow current policies.

documentation: Approved plan of operation with signature page
LIC 999 sketches
Job descriptions and personnel policies (LIC 281, B4–B5) and night shift duty statement
Document control log and archived versions
Staff policy acknowledgments
Annual review records

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Internal Compliance Review (facility-adopted; no state QAPI mandate verified)
policies.applies_to: Administrator, governing body, designated staff reviewers
policies.purpose: To give [AGENCY NAME] a regular internal review that finds and corrects compliance gaps before a CDSS inspection and improves resident care.
policies.policy: No mandatory quality assurance and performance improvement (QAPI) program for RCFEs was found in the verified California sources. [AGENCY NAME] has voluntarily adopted this internal compliance review as good practice. It is not a regulatory requirement. The administrator conducts quarterly mock inspections of medication records, personnel files and resident files against Title 22 and records, corrects and follows up on all findings. The facility also tracks CDSS deficiencies and plans of correction to closure.

definitions.definition: A scheduled internal review that uses the same standards a CDSS evaluator would use.
A written plan, with dates and responsible persons, to fix a deficiency cited by CDSS or found internally.
The running record of all findings, actions, owners, due dates and completion dates.

procedures: The administrator schedules a mock inspection each quarter and records the dates for the year on a compliance calendar.

Medication review: a reviewer checks centrally stored medications for locked storage, original containers, PRN orders with the required content, medication records and destruction records against 22 CCR §87465. The reviewer samples at least [NUMBER] residents each quarter.
Personnel review: a reviewer checks each personnel file for training documentation, first aid, health screening, criminal record clearance or exemption, and the other items required by 22 CCR §87411.

Resident file review: a reviewer checks that each resident file has a pre-admission appraisal, a current reassessment and a signed admission agreement within 7 days of admission that meets 22 CCR §87507.
The reviewer completes a written checklist for each area, noting compliant, non-compliant or not applicable, with evidence.
The administrator reviews the infection control plan at least annually and updates it for any new hazard or change in practice.
The administrator reviews the facility's incident reports, grievances, falls and unusual occurrences each quarter to identify patterns, such as repeated falls or medication errors.
Each finding is entered in the corrective action log with an owner and due date. Findings involving resident safety are corrected immediately. Other findings are corrected within 30 days.
When CDSS cites a deficiency, the administrator enters it in the log and completes the plan of correction by the date CDSS specifies. The administrator keeps proof of correction.
The administrator re-checks corrected items at the next quarterly review to confirm the correction held.
The administrator presents a summary of findings, trends and corrective actions to the governing body each quarter and the governing body records its review and any direction in minutes.
The administrator may share de-identified results with staff at meetings and uses them to plan training.
The facility reviews this policy annually and does not describe it to residents, families or regulators as a state-mandated QAPI program.

responsibilities.duty: Schedule and conduct reviews, maintain the corrective action log, complete CDSS plans of correction and report to the governing body.
Review quarterly results and ensure resources for corrections.
Cooperate with reviews and carry out assigned corrections.

documentation: Compliance calendar
Quarterly mock inspection checklists
Corrective action log
CDSS deficiency notices and plans of correction with proof of correction
Annual infection control plan review record
Governing body minutes

policies.title: False Claims, Advertising Accuracy and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, marketing and billing staff
federal: 42 CFR 441.301(c) (only if enrolled in the Assisted Living Waiver)
policies.purpose: To ensure that everything [AGENCY NAME] tells the public about its services, and everything it charges residents or payers, is truthful, authorized and documented.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not make false or misleading claims in advertising, marketing, admission materials or billing. Advertisements describe only services the facility actually provides and is licensed to provide. A facility that advertises dementia care has a written dementia program meeting 22 CCR §87706 and keeps its advertisements for 3 years. A separate charge is imposed only if it is listed in and authorized by the admission agreement (22 CCR §87507), and each resident receives an itemized monthly statement. If the facility participates in the Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver, waiver services are billed only through DHCS-enrolled provider channels, and residents pay their own room and board.

definitions.definition: Any website, brochure, sign, listing, social media post, referral-source material or oral marketing statement about the facility.
Any advertising that states or implies the facility provides dementia, memory or Alzheimer's care.
A fee for an additional service that is not part of the basic rate and that must be listed in the admission agreement.
A monthly written statement showing each charge, payment and balance.

procedures: The administrator reviews and approves every advertisement and marketing statement before release. The review checks that each claim about services, staffing, licensure, levels of care and price is accurate and supportable.

Advertising does not state or imply services the facility does not provide, a license type it does not hold, or staff qualifications it does not have. The administrator corrects or withdraws inaccurate material immediately.

Before any advertisement says the facility provides dementia, memory or Alzheimer's care, the administrator confirms that a written dementia program exists covering philosophy, admission, training, activities, environment, changes in condition and success indicators (22 CCR §87706).
The administrator keeps a dated copy of every advertisement, including dementia care advertising, for at least 3 years in the advertising file.

Marketing staff give prospective residents the admission agreement, rate information and the facility's description of basic and additional services in plain language before the agreement is signed. Verbal statements must match the written agreement.

The facility charges a separate fee only when the fee is listed in and authorized by the signed admission agreement. If a service is not in the agreement, the facility does not charge for it until the agreement is amended with the resident's or representative's written consent.

Billing staff prepare an itemized monthly statement of charges for each resident, showing the basic rate, each additional service charge, payments received and balance. Statements go to the resident or representative on a fixed day each month.
Billing staff do not alter, back-date or round charges and do not bill for services not delivered. A second person (the administrator) reviews the statements before they are released.
Rate changes follow the notice requirements of the admission agreement and 22 CCR §87507, including 60 days' written notice. Billing staff do not apply a new rate before the notice period ends.

If the facility is enrolled in the Assisted Living Waiver, waiver services are billed only through DHCS-enrolled provider channels. Staff do not bill a resident or family for any waiver-covered service, and the resident is charged only for room and board and other items permitted by the agreement and waiver rules. 42 CFR 441.301(c) requirements for home and community-based settings are followed.
Billing staff keep service delivery records that support every claim and compare them to billing monthly.

Any employee who believes an advertisement, charge or claim is false or inaccurate reports it to the administrator. The administrator investigates within 5 business days, corrects the problem, refunds any overcharge promptly, and records the outcome. No employee is punished for making a good-faith report.
The administrator audits advertising and billing at least quarterly as part of the internal compliance review.

responsibilities.duty: Approve advertising, maintain the dementia program if advertised, review billing, investigate reports and refund overcharges.
Use only approved materials, charge only authorized fees and issue accurate itemized statements.
Set the rate structure, support correction of errors and oversee waiver enrollment where applicable.
Report suspected false claims or billing errors.

documentation: Advertising file with dated copies kept at least 3 years
Written dementia program (if advertised)
Signed admission agreements and amendments
Itemized monthly statements
Rate change notices
Service delivery records matched to billing
Records of reports, investigations and refunds
DHCS enrollment and billing records (if enrolled in the Assisted Living Waiver)

policies.title: Liability Insurance, Workers' Compensation and Bonding
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, and the person responsible for business and financial records
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] carries the insurance and bonding California requires of a Residential Care Facility for the Elderly (RCFE), so that residents, guests and employees are protected and the facility can show proof at any time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 in the aggregate for injury to residents and guests caused by negligence of the licensee, as required by HSC §1569.605. [AGENCY NAME] carries workers' compensation insurance for all employees as soon as it has any employees. If [AGENCY NAME] ever holds resident cash, it first completes the LIC 400 affidavit and obtains the LIC 402 surety bond, and it handles the money only as §87217 requires. Coverage is never allowed to lapse while the facility is licensed. If coverage cannot be shown, the Administrator must not admit new residents and must immediately notify the Licensee.

definitions.definition: The most the liability policy will pay for a single event. For this facility the minimum is $1,000,000.
The most the liability policy will pay for all claims in the policy period. For this facility the minimum is $3,000,000.
Insurance that pays medical care and wage benefits to employees injured or made ill by their work.
A bond that protects resident money held by the facility. It is filed together with the LIC 400 affidavit.
Money belonging to a resident that the facility holds or manages on the resident's behalf.

procedures: Before the license application is submitted, the Licensee obtains quotes from licensed insurers for a facility liability policy with limits of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 aggregate, and confirms in writing that the policy covers injury to residents and guests caused by negligence.
The Licensee binds the liability policy before any resident is admitted. The Administrator files the declarations page and certificate of insurance in the Governance binder.
The Administrator checks the declarations page against the required limits and records the policy number, insurer, limits and expiration date on the Insurance and Bonding Tracking Log.

Before the first employee starts work, the Licensee binds a workers' compensation policy. The Administrator files the certificate in the Governance binder and posts the workers' compensation notice in the employee area, as the insurer directs.
The Administrator confirms each year that payroll and job classifications reported to the workers' compensation carrier match the actual staff, and corrects any difference with the carrier.
The Administrator sets a calendar reminder 90 days before each policy expiration. At 60 days the Administrator contacts the broker to renew. At 30 days the renewal declarations page must be in hand.

The Licensee reviews coverage whenever capacity, services or building use change, and also when the facility adds a van or other vehicle. The Licensee gives the broker written notice of the change before it takes effect.

The facility does not hold resident cash by default. The Administrator may allow it only after written approval from the Licensee and only after the LIC 400 affidavit is completed and the LIC 402 surety bond is in force.

If resident cash will be held, the Administrator submits the LIC 400 and LIC 402 to the licensing agency, keeps copies in the Governance binder, and documents the bond number, amount and expiration date on the tracking log.
If resident cash is held, the Administrator opens a separate account titled as the residents' money. Resident funds are never combined with facility operating funds or staff personal funds.

For every deposit or withdrawal of resident cash, staff issue a receipt and enter it in the resident's accounting record. The Administrator reconciles the account to the records monthly and initials the reconciliation.

If the bond is cancelled, lapses or is not renewed, the Administrator stops holding resident cash on the same day. The Administrator gives each resident or representative a full accounting and returns the money, and notifies the licensing agency.

When an incident occurs that may lead to a liability or workers' compensation claim, the Administrator notifies the insurer or broker within 24 hours, or sooner if the policy requires. The Administrator keeps a copy of the notice with the incident report (see SAF-02).
The Administrator gives proof of insurance to the licensing agency, the Ombudsman, or a resident or representative who asks for it, within 2 business days.
The Licensee reviews the Insurance and Bonding Tracking Log at least quarterly and signs it. Any gap in coverage is corrected the same day and noted in the Quality Assurance review (see GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Buys and keeps required coverage, approves any decision to hold resident cash, and reviews the tracking log quarterly.
Verifies limits, tracks expiration dates, files certificates, notifies insurers of incidents, and manages the bond and resident cash accounting if applicable.
Keeps receipts and account reconciliation for any resident cash and does not commingle funds.

documentation: Liability insurance declarations page and certificates of insurance
Workers' compensation certificate and payroll classification records
Insurance and Bonding Tracking Log
LIC 400 affidavit and LIC 402 surety bond (only if resident cash is held)
Separate resident-funds account statements, receipts and monthly reconciliations (only if resident cash is held)
Insurer notification records for incidents

policies.title: Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver Participation and HCBS Settings Compliance (applies only if enrolled)
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, Resident Care Staff and any staff who help arrange Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver (ALW) services. This policy applies only if [AGENCY NAME] is enrolled, or is applying to enroll, as an ALW provider.
policies.purpose: To set the rules for ALW participation, if the facility chooses to participate, and for meeting the federal Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) settings requirements, so that participants live in a setting that protects privacy, choice, and access to food and visitors.
policies.policy: Participation in the Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver is voluntary and does not change [AGENCY NAME]'s duties under its RCFE license. If [AGENCY NAME] enrolls, it complies with the HCBS settings requirements in 42 CFR 441.301(c). That means each participant has a lease or residency agreement, privacy, choice, and access to food and visitors. This policy is inactive unless the Licensee enrolls the facility with the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS). Participation is allowed only in the counties where ALW operates and only after DHCS enrollment is complete.

definitions.definition: A Medi-Cal program run by DHCS that pays for assisted living services for eligible participants. It operates only in 15 counties.
Federal standards (42 CFR 441.301(c)) for where Medicaid home and community-based services are delivered. They include a lease or agreement, privacy, resident choice, and access to food and visitors.
The daily ALW service rate, from Tier 1 at $95.69 to Tier 5 at $270.80 per day. It does not cover room and board.
The monthly room and board amount for SSI/SSP residents. It is currently $1,444.07 a month.
An emergency response system for participants. It is required when a facility has more than 6 ALW participants.

procedures: The Licensee decides in writing whether to enroll in the ALW and records the decision in the Governing Body minutes. If the decision is no, the Administrator notes 'Not enrolled' on the Governance checklist and no further steps apply.

Before applying, the Administrator confirms the facility is in one of the 15 ALW counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, Fresno, Kern, Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, Sacramento, San Bernardino, San Diego, San Francisco, San Joaquin, San Mateo, Santa Clara or Sonoma.

The Administrator contacts DHCS at ProFacWAIVER@dhcs.ca.gov and WaiveProEnroll@dhcs.ca.gov to request the current provider enrollment packet and to confirm requirements. The Administrator documents the date and response.
The Administrator budgets for the CY2026 application fee of $750 included in the Medi-Cal enrollment packet, and keeps proof of payment with the application.
The Licensee confirms before enrolling that licensed nursing staff will be on call or employed, as ALW providers need. The Administrator documents the nurse's name, license number and arrangement.

If the facility will serve more than 6 ALW participants, the Administrator arranges an Individual Response System before the seventh participant is admitted and records the vendor, installation date and testing schedule.

The Administrator explains to each applicant and representative that the ALW pays the tier rate and does not pay room and board. The Administrator gives a written breakdown of room and board charges. For SSI/SSP participants, room and board is the SSI/SSP basic services rate of $1,444.07 a month, and the resident keeps the personal needs amount.

Each participant signs the admission agreement (see RR-04) as a lease or residency agreement. It states the services, rates, eviction grounds and notice rights, and the right to contact CDSS and the Ombudsman.
Staff protect each participant's privacy. Participants keep control of their rooms and personal space, may use a phone in private, and receive mail unopened (see RR-01 and RR-07).

The Administrator makes sure participants make their own choices about daily routines, activities and who provides care, within the limits of the licensing regulations and the individual service plan (see ADM-03).
Participants have access to food at all times of day as set out in the food service policy, and are not limited to meal times alone (see DL-01).

Participants may have visitors at any time of their choosing, subject only to the posted visiting policy and any documented, individually assessed reason that is consistent with the licensing regulations (see SAF-08).

Any proposed restriction on privacy, choice, food access or visitors for a participant must be reviewed by the Administrator, discussed with the participant and representative, and documented in the individual service plan before it is put in place. No blanket facility-wide restriction is allowed.

Each year, the Administrator audits a sample of participant records and observes daily routines against the four HCBS elements (agreement, privacy, choice, food and visitor access). Findings go to the Licensee and into the Quality Assurance review (see GOV-05).

The Administrator follows any DHCS notice about electronic visit verification or other waiver reporting. The facility does not assume that electronic visit verification applies to RCFE residential services unless DHCS says in writing that it does.

If the facility disenrolls or loses ALW status, the Administrator tells participants and representatives in writing at least 60 days ahead, or as soon as DHCS allows, and follows the transfer and notice rules in ADM-06.

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether to enroll, funds the application fee and required nursing and response systems, and receives the annual HCBS audit.
Manages DHCS enrollment, rate and billing documents, HCBS audits, and approves any individual restriction.
Provides nursing oversight required by ALW for participants.
Honor privacy, choice, food access and visitor access for every participant, and report concerns to the Administrator.

documentation: Governing Body decision on ALW enrollment
DHCS correspondence and enrollment packet, with the $750 application fee receipt
Nurse on-call or employment documentation
Individual Response System contract and test records (if more than 6 participants)
Participant admission agreements and room and board breakdowns
Individual restriction reviews and consent notes
Annual HCBS settings audit and corrective action plans

policies.title: Resident Personal Rights and Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: All residents and representatives, and all staff, volunteers and contractors
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident of [AGENCY NAME] is told about, and can use, every one of the 18 personal rights in 22 CCR §87468.1(a), and that staff are trained to protect them.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] respects and implements every personal right in 22 CCR §87468.1(a). Residents are treated with dignity. They are free from punishment, humiliation, intimidation and abuse. They may leave at any time and are never locked in. They may keep and spend their own money, keep personal possessions with individual storage space, make confidential phone calls, receive unopened mail, vote, accept or refuse medical care, and move out. Ombudsmen and advocates may visit them privately during reasonable hours without prior notice. No house rule may limit a right unless the Department has given written permission. Residents are also asked to follow the reasonable house rules in the admission agreement. Failure to do so does not remove their rights.

definitions.definition: The 18 rights listed in 22 CCR §87468.1(a) that every RCFE resident holds.
A person legally authorized or designated by the resident to act on the resident's behalf.
A written rule of the facility that applies to residents, such as quiet hours or visiting hours.
A Long-Term Care Ombudsman representative who advocates for residents and may visit privately.

procedures: The Administrator keeps a current copy of the personal rights in §87468.1(a) and the notice format used by the Department, and keeps them available to staff, residents and the public.

At or before admission, the Administrator or designee reads and explains the personal rights to the resident and representative in plain language, and in the resident's language where needed (see RR-08). The resident or representative signs and dates an acknowledgment that is kept in the resident file.
The Administrator gives each resident and representative a written copy of the rights and posts the rights in a prominent common area where residents and visitors can read them.

The Administrator tells each resident and representative how to make a complaint, including the address and phone number of the CCLD complaint unit and how to reach the Ombudsman, and records this in the acknowledgment (see RR-02, RR-03).

Staff respect dignity at all times. Staff knock before entering a room, address residents by their preferred name, provide personal care in private, and never use punishment, humiliation, intimidation or threats.

The Administrator does not lock exterior doors in a way that prevents residents from leaving, and does not impose house rules such as locking doors at night or barring windows without the Department's permission under §87468.1(a)(6). Any request to the Department is made in writing and filed.
Residents may keep and spend their own money. The facility does not require a resident to turn over funds. Staff offer help with funds only under the resident funds policy (see RR-05).

Each resident has individual storage space for personal possessions. Staff do not enter or search storage without the resident's permission, except in an emergency or as the law allows, and document the reason.
Residents may make and receive confidential phone calls. Staff give residents access to a phone in a private location and hand over mail unopened.

Staff support each resident's right to accept or reject medical care. A refusal is documented, the physician and representative are told, and the Administrator reviews any effect on the individual service plan (see ADM-03, HCS-05).
On request or before each election, staff help residents register and vote, and keep a record of the help given.

Ombudsmen, advocacy representatives and licensing staff are admitted for private visits at reasonable hours without prior notice (see RR-03). Staff do not ask them to wait for permission or stay in the room.
Staff do not restrict any right based on a resident's actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status (see RR-08).

Within the first 30 days of employment, and again annually, the Administrator trains each staff member on resident rights, in line with the training required under §87411. The trainer, date, content and staff signature are placed in the personnel file (see STF-03).

Staff who see a violation of a resident's rights report it to the Administrator immediately. The Administrator investigates the same day, takes corrective action, and records the result. Reports of abuse follow SAF-01.
The Administrator reviews complaints, incident reports and resident council input quarterly for rights concerns and records trends and corrections in the Quality Assurance review (see GOV-05, RR-09).

responsibilities.duty: Adopts this policy and does not adopt any house rule that conflicts with the personal rights.
Delivers and posts the rights, obtains acknowledgments, seeks Department permission before any restriction, and investigates alleged violations.
Honor each right in daily care, complete rights training, and report suspected violations immediately.
Are asked to follow reasonable house rules and to raise concerns through the grievance process.

documentation: Signed acknowledgment of personal rights in each resident file
Posted personal rights notice
Department permission letters for any restricted house rule
Staff rights training records in personnel files
Records of voting help and refused care
Rights violation investigation notes and corrective actions

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints (resident and neighborhood)
policies.applies_to: Residents, representatives, family, neighbors, Administrator and all staff
policies.purpose: To give residents, representatives and neighbors a clear, safe way to raise concerns and have them resolved promptly, without fear of retaliation.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] welcomes complaints and treats each one seriously. The admission agreement states the grievance procedure and the resident's right to contact CDSS and the Ombudsman. Residents are told how to confidentially register a complaint with CCLD, including the address and phone number of the complaint receiving unit. Communications from representatives are answered promptly. The facility specifies how residents may suggest changes to policy. If the owner does not live in a home serving 6 or fewer residents, [AGENCY NAME] also keeps a neighborhood complaint policy as required by LIC 281 attachment B15. No resident, representative or staff member is punished, threatened or treated differently for making a complaint.

definitions.definition: Any complaint or concern raised by a resident or representative about care, services, staff, other residents, rights or the facility.
A complaint from a neighbor about noise, parking, traffic, property upkeep or other effects of the facility on the surrounding area.
Any adverse action taken because someone made, or helped with, a complaint.
The unit of Community Care Licensing that takes confidential complaints about facilities.

procedures: At admission, the Administrator explains the grievance procedure to the resident and representative and gives a written copy. This is also stated in the admission agreement, together with the right to contact CDSS and the Ombudsman (see RR-04).

The Administrator gives each resident and representative the address and phone number of the CCLD complaint receiving unit and the Ombudsman, and posts them in a common area with the Ombudsman CRISISline 1-800-231-4024 and the local Ombudsman number (see RR-03).

A resident or representative may complain orally or in writing to any staff member, the Administrator, the Licensee, the Ombudsman or CCLD. Staff who receive a complaint accept it, thank the person, and give it to the Administrator the same day.

The Administrator (or [ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) enters the complaint on the Grievance Log with the date, name, summary and any immediate risk to a resident. If the complaint involves suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, the Administrator follows SAF-01 immediately.
The Administrator acknowledges the complaint to the resident or representative within 1 business day, and answers representative communications promptly.

The Administrator investigates by interviewing the people involved, reviewing records and observing where needed. The Administrator aims to resolve the complaint and give a written response within 10 calendar days. If more time is needed, the Administrator tells the complainant why and when to expect an answer.

The written response states what was found, what action was taken, and that the complainant may contact CCLD or the Ombudsman if not satisfied. The Administrator records the outcome and the date on the Grievance Log.

A resident may ask that a complaint be kept confidential. The Administrator limits the information shared to those who need it to resolve the issue, and does not reveal the complainant's name unless required by law.

The Administrator never allows retaliation. No resident is moved, denied services, discharged or threatened because of a complaint, and no employee is disciplined for reporting. Any retaliation allegation is investigated at once and may lead to discipline up to termination.

Residents may suggest changes to facility policy through the Resident Council or by giving a written or oral suggestion to the Administrator. The Administrator reviews suggestions at the next monthly management meeting and tells the resident the decision (see RR-09, GOV-04).

If the owner does not live in the home and the home serves 6 or fewer residents, or if the facility is otherwise subject to LIC 281 attachment B15, the Administrator keeps and follows the Neighborhood Complaint Procedure in steps 12 to 14.

The Administrator gives neighbors a phone number and e-mail address, [PHONE] and [ADDRESS], where complaints can be made, and may post this at the entrance or give it in writing to adjacent properties on request.

The Administrator acknowledges a neighborhood complaint within 2 business days, looks into the matter, corrects any problem within the facility's control (for example noise, parking or trash), and replies in writing or by phone. The result is entered on the Grievance Log.
The Administrator gives the Licensee a summary of all grievances and neighborhood complaints every quarter, with trends and corrections, for the Quality Assurance review (see GOV-05).
If the facility is enrolled in the Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver, the Administrator also makes sure that participants' choice and privacy complaints are reviewed under GOV-08.

responsibilities.duty: Receives, logs, investigates and answers all complaints and prevents retaliation.
Accept any complaint without judgment, pass it to the Administrator the same day, and never retaliate.
Reviews the quarterly complaint summary and supports corrective action.
Brings resident concerns and policy suggestions to the Administrator.

documentation: Grievance Log with dates, findings, responses and outcomes
Written responses to complainants
Posted notice with CCLD, Ombudsman and CRISISline contacts
Neighborhood Complaint Procedure (LIC 281 attachment B15), if applicable
Quarterly complaint trend summary

policies.title: Long-Term Care Ombudsman and Licensing Agency Access
policies.applies_to: Administrator, all staff, residents and representatives
federal: Older Americans Act (45 CFR 1324 Subpart A)
policies.purpose: To make sure Ombudsmen, advocates and licensing staff have prompt and private access to residents and records, and that the facility makes the required notices and reports to them.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] allows Long-Term Care Ombudsmen and resident advocacy representatives to visit residents privately, during reasonable hours, without prior notice, as 22 CCR §87468.1(a)(11) requires. The facility posts the CRISISline 1-800-231-4024 and the local Ombudsman number. The facility sends written notice to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman within 2 business days of any foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default or utility shut-off notice, as §87211(d) requires. Suspected abuse is reported to the local Ombudsman, the licensing agency and local law enforcement as §87211(b) and (c) require. The admission agreement states the Department's authority to examine resident records.

definitions.definition: A program representative of the California Department of Aging who advocates for residents and receives complaints and abuse reports.
A person acting for a recognized advocacy organization who is entitled to meet privately with residents.
The statewide 24-hour Ombudsman line, 1-800-231-4024.
CDSS Community Care Licensing Division, Adult and Senior Care Program.

procedures: The Administrator posts in a common area the CRISISline 1-800-231-4024, the local Ombudsman name and number, and the CCLD contact information. The Administrator checks the notice each month to make sure it is readable and current.
The Administrator tells every resident and representative at admission, and in the admission agreement, of the right to contact CDSS and the Ombudsman (see RR-04).
Staff are trained at hire and annually that Ombudsmen and advocates may visit at any reasonable hour without notice and without asking permission (see STF-03).

When an Ombudsman or advocate arrives, staff greet the visitor, ask for identification, tell the Administrator or person in charge, and let the visitor meet residents. Staff do not ask the purpose of the visit.
Visits are private. Staff do not remain in the room, listen, or ask the resident afterward what was said. A resident may decline a visit, and the resident's choice is respected.
The Administrator records each visit, with the date, time, name and organization, on the Visitor and Agency Log. The log does not record what the resident discussed.
The Administrator cooperates with Ombudsman and licensing requests to review records the Department is authorized to examine, and gives access promptly. The admission agreement states this authority.

When a licensing inspector arrives, staff notify the Administrator, provide access to all areas and requested records, and do not delay. The Administrator keeps a copy of any visit report or deficiency notice.

If the Administrator or any staff member suspects physical abuse of an elder or dependent adult, the person reports to the local Ombudsman, the licensing agency and local law enforcement. This is done within 2 hours if there is serious bodily injury, and otherwise within 24 hours. This is in addition to the duties in SAF-01.

For a death, serious injury, AED use or other incident threatening health, safety or welfare, the Administrator sends the written report to the licensing agency and the person responsible for the resident within 7 days (see SAF-02, REC-02).

If the facility receives a foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default or utility shut-off notice, the Administrator gives written notice to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman within 2 business days, and also notifies the licensing agency as the regulation requires. The date sent and a copy go into the Governance binder.
The Administrator checks incoming mail and e-mail daily for these notices, and tells the Licensee on the day they arrive so the 2-business-day deadline is met.
The Administrator follows up on Ombudsman recommendations within 10 calendar days, documents the action taken, and tells the Ombudsman the result if requested.
Staff and the Administrator must never discourage, retaliate against, or punish any resident or employee for contact with the Ombudsman or licensing agency.
The Administrator reviews the Visitor and Agency Log and all reports to agencies every quarter for the Quality Assurance review (see GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Posts contacts, grants access, makes required reports and notices on time, and documents agency visits.
Let Ombudsmen and advocates in without delay, protect privacy, and report suspected abuse immediately.
Makes sure financial default notices are passed to the Administrator and reported within 2 business days.

documentation: Posted Ombudsman and CRISISline notice
Visitor and Agency Log
Copies of the 2-business-day financial notices to the State Ombudsman
Abuse reports to the Ombudsman, licensing and law enforcement
Licensing visit reports and responses
Ombudsman follow-up records

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Preadmission Fees, Rate Changes and Refunds
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, staff who handle admissions and billing, residents and representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident signs a clear, lawful admission agreement and is charged, notified and refunded fairly in line with 22 CCR §87507.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] enters an individual written admission agreement with every resident. The agreement is in 12-point black type on plain white paper, one-sided, in plain language, with titled sections. It is signed and dated by the resident or representative and the licensee within 7 days of admission, and a copy is given immediately.
