Staff must tell the administrator promptly if they develop a physical illness, TB symptoms or an emotional condition that could affect resident safety. No staff member is penalized for making a good-faith report.

If the administrator has reason to believe a staff member's physical illness or emotional instability poses a significant threat to residents, the administrator immediately relieves the person of duty, documents the reason, and does not return the person to duty until a physician states in writing that the person is able to work safely.

For staff with possible exposure to blood or body fluids, the administrator provides bloodborne pathogen training and protective equipment as required by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030, and records the training in the personnel file.

Health screening reports are filed in the personnel record and are shown only to the administrator, the licensee, and CDSS Licensing staff on request. Health information is not shared with other staff or residents.

responsibilities.duty: Provides time and resources for screening and ensures the administrator enforces this policy.
Collects and reviews all screening reports, keeps the tracking log, relieves staff of duty when a significant threat exists, and files all records.
Complete screening within the required window, report new health conditions, and follow any restrictions from a physician or health officer.
Sign the statement of good health before starting.

documentation: Signed physician health screening report (LIC 503 or equivalent) for each person
TB test or chest x-ray result
Volunteer statement of good health
Personnel health screening tracking log
Record of any relief from duty and physician clearance to return
Bloodborne pathogen training record

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: Administrator, licensee, human resources designee, and all personnel
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete, accurate and available personnel record for every person who works or is present in the facility, so that a CDSS Licensing surveyor can verify training, health screening and criminal record clearance on request.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a separate personnel record for each employee, including the licensee and administrator, and a file for each volunteer. The record contains the personnel record form (LIC 501 or equivalent), the physician health screening report, criminal record clearance or exemption documentation, evidence of training including sign-in sheets, and the other items required by Title 22 for personnel records. Training documentation is kept in the personnel record as 22 CCR §87411 requires. Records are kept current, are available for review by CDSS Licensing, and are kept in a secure location. No person works or is present in the facility until criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer is documented.

definitions.definition: The file kept for each employee that documents qualifications, health screening, criminal record clearance and training.
DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance, exemption, or an approved transfer, as required by 22 CCR §87355 and §87411.
A dated record showing the topic, hours, trainer name and qualifications, and the signatures of those who attended.

procedures: Before the first day of work, the administrator opens a personnel record for each new hire and a file for each volunteer.

The administrator completes or collects the personnel record form (LIC 501 or equivalent) showing name, address, date of hire, position, and date of birth. The administrator also records date of birth to verify minimum age (anyone supervising staff or residents must be 18 or older).

The administrator verifies and files proof that the person is at least the required age for the position and that the person has the qualifications for the job. For the administrator, this includes the certificate described in STF-02 and GOV-02.

The administrator files the criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer documentation (see STF-02) before the person begins work or is present in the facility. A person without documented clearance does not work or stay in the facility.
The administrator files the physician health screening report (LIC 503 or equivalent) and TB test or x-ray result within the time limits in STF-04.

The administrator files all training documentation in the personnel record, including initial training, annual training, first aid and CPR certificates, and dementia, medication assistance and resident rights training.

For each training session the trainer or administrator keeps a sign-in sheet with the date, topic, hours, trainer name and qualifications. A copy of the sheet or a certificate is placed in each attendee's personnel record.
The administrator files signed acknowledgments of this manual's key policies, including resident rights, abuse reporting and confidentiality, with the date signed.
The administrator files any signed job description, disciplinary action, performance evaluation and separation notice in the personnel record.
The administrator keeps personnel records in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system that only the administrator, licensee and designated HR staff can open.

The administrator audits all personnel records at least every 6 months, using a checklist covering clearance, health screening, training hours, first aid and CPR expiration, and form completion. The administrator corrects any gap within 7 days.
The administrator keeps an index of current staff with training due dates and certificate expirations, and reviews it monthly.

Personnel records are made available to CDSS Licensing during inspections and on request. Records of former employees are kept as required by Title 22 and California employment law. Before destroying any record of a former employee, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms the required retention period with CDSS Licensing or legal counsel.
When a staff member leaves, the administrator completes a separation entry in the record, retrieves keys, access codes and badges, and does not discard any record.

responsibilities.duty: Creates, completes, audits and secures all personnel records and makes them available to Licensing.
Ensures resources for record keeping and reviews audit results.
Provide accurate information, submit training certificates and health documents, and report changes of name or address.
Complete sign-in sheets with topic, hours and qualifications.

documentation: Personnel record form (LIC 501 or equivalent)
Physician health screening report (LIC 503 or equivalent) and TB result
Criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer documentation (LIC 508 where applicable)
Training sign-in sheets and certificates, including first aid and CPR
Signed policy acknowledgments
Personnel record audit checklist and staff training index

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, volunteers, contractors and the administrator
policies.purpose: To set clear standards for how staff treat residents and each other, so that every resident is treated with dignity and the personal rights in 22 CCR §87468.1 are protected, and to maintain professional boundaries between staff and residents.
policies.policy: All staff treat each resident with dignity and respect. Staff do not punish, humiliate, intimidate or abuse residents, and do not withhold a resident's money. Staff do not discriminate against any resident, applicant or visitor on the basis of actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status, and staff use each resident's preferred name and pronouns. Staff receive training on residents' rights. Residents are never used as substitutes for required staff. Because no state-specific gift or boundary rule was verified, [AGENCY NAME] applies the facility standards set out in this policy. Violations result in corrective action up to and including termination and, where required, a report to authorities.

definitions.definition: The limit that separates a staff member's professional role from personal, financial or social involvement with a resident.
Any action taken to punish a resident, including withholding food, activities, visits, money or care, or humiliating or isolating the resident.
The name and pronouns a resident asks to be used, whether or not they match legal or birth records.

procedures: At hire and before working with residents, each staff member receives this policy and the Resident Personal Rights policy (RR-01), signs an acknowledgment, and is trained on residents' rights as part of initial training.
Staff address residents by their preferred name and pronouns. Staff record the preferred name and pronouns in the resident's file with the resident's consent and tell co-workers who need to know.
Staff knock and wait for permission before entering a resident's room, except in an emergency, and provide personal care with privacy.

Staff never use physical force, threats, yelling, ridicule, mocking, name-calling or any form of punishment or intimidation with a resident. Staff never withhold food, care, activities, visitors, phone, mail or the resident's own money as discipline.

Staff do not deny or change admission, room or restroom assignment, room sharing, transfer, discharge, or association with others because of actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status.

Staff do not borrow money from, sell to, or buy from residents. Staff do not accept gifts of cash from residents. Staff may accept small tokens of appreciation such as food or cards valued under $25 if they report them to the administrator the same day. The administrator logs them.

Staff do not accept any gift, bequest, power of attorney, joint account, loan or role as beneficiary from a resident or the resident's family without the administrator's written approval after consulting legal counsel.

Staff do not have romantic or sexual relationships with residents, and do not share personal social media contact with residents. Staff do not post photos or information about residents on social media or any public platform.
Staff do not use residents' belongings, vehicles or phones for personal use, and do not run personal errands for residents on their own time without the administrator's approval.

Staff do not use residents to perform staff duties or to stand in for staff. Residents may volunteer for personal activities only when they want to and when it is not a substitute for required staffing. The administrator documents any such arrangement.
Staff do not discuss their personal religious, political or personal beliefs with residents in a way that pressures them.

Staff must immediately report any suspected violation of this policy, or any suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, to the administrator. They must also report suspected abuse as required by SAF-01. No retaliation is allowed against any person who reports in good faith.
The administrator investigates every report promptly, separates the staff member and resident if needed for safety, interviews witnesses, and documents findings within 5 days.

The administrator takes corrective action consistent with the findings, which may include retraining, suspension or termination, and makes any report required to CDSS Licensing, the ombudsman, law enforcement or the Adult Protective Services agency (see SAF-01 and REC-02).
The administrator reviews resident rights and professional boundaries with all staff at least annually and whenever a violation occurs, and documents attendance.

responsibilities.duty: Trains staff, investigates reports, applies corrective action and makes required reports.
Follow this policy, use preferred names and pronouns, avoid boundary violations and report concerns immediately.
Supports enforcement and reviews any substantiated violation.

documentation: Signed staff acknowledgment of this policy and RR-01
Resident rights training sign-in sheets
Gift log
Investigation notes and corrective action records
Records of any reports made to outside agencies

policies.title: Wage-Hour, Paid Sick Leave and Meal/Rest Rules (CA-specific addition)
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, payroll designee, and all employees
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] pays employees at least the legal minimum wage, provides paid sick leave, and follows meal and rest period rules that apply to 24-hour residential care for the elderly. Unpaid wages and missed breaks are common sources of claims against small care homes.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] pays every non-exempt employee at least the highest applicable minimum wage, pays overtime as required, provides at least 40 hours or 5 days of paid sick leave per year as required by Labor Code §246, and follows the meal and rest period rules of IWC Wage Order 5 for 24-hour residential care for the elderly. Live-in and 24-hour shifts are not scheduled until the licensee has obtained advice from employment counsel. Employees are classified as exempt only when they meet every legal test, including the salary threshold. The licensee does not rely on this policy as legal advice and consults employment counsel on classification and scheduling questions.

definitions.definition: The state rate of $16.90 per hour from January 1, 2026, or the higher local rate where the facility is located.
Paid time off that employees earn and use for their own or a family member's health care needs, with at least 40 hours or 5 days available per year under Labor Code §246.
An employee who meets every legal test for exemption, including duties and a minimum salary. The minimum annual salary for exempt managers is $70,304.
The IWC wage order covering the public housekeeping industry, which includes residential care for the elderly.

procedures: Before hiring, the licensee confirms the minimum wage that applies at the facility's address. The state rate is $16.90 per hour from January 1, 2026. Higher local rates include City of Los Angeles $18.42 and San Francisco $19.61 from July 1, 2026, San Diego $17.75 and San Jose $18.45. The licensee verifies current local rates each January and July.
The payroll designee sets every non-exempt employee's pay rate at or above the highest applicable minimum wage and records the rate on the offer letter and in payroll.

The licensee classifies each position as exempt or non-exempt in writing. A position is exempt only if the duties test is met and the salary is at least $70,304 per year for managers. Direct care staff, cooks, housekeepers and relief staff are treated as non-exempt unless employment counsel advises otherwise in writing.

Non-exempt employees record their actual start and stop times, including meal periods, using the facility time system. Employees may not work off the clock. Supervisors do not ask employees to work unrecorded time.

The payroll designee pays overtime and any premium pay required by California law and the federal home care rule for hours over the legal thresholds. The payroll designee reviews each pay period before payroll is processed.

Each employee earns and can use paid sick leave of at least 40 hours or 5 days per year as required by Labor Code §246. The payroll designee tracks accrual and use and lists the balance on each pay statement or in a separate written notice.

Employees may request paid sick leave orally or in writing. The administrator does not require an employee to find a replacement as a condition of using sick leave, and does not retaliate against any employee for using it.
The administrator posts the required wage and hour notices and gives every new hire written notice of pay rate, pay day and sick leave terms at hire.

The administrator schedules meal and rest periods for each shift in line with IWC Wage Order 5. For a sole caregiver in 24-hour residential care for the elderly, the administrator follows the special meal and rest period rules in the wage order. The administrator documents how residents are supervised during the employee's break so that resident safety is maintained.

The licensee does not set up any live-in, 24-hour or sleep-time shift until the licensee has obtained advice from employment counsel on pay, meal and rest periods, and overtime. The licensee keeps the written advice on file.
Where an employee does not receive a required meal or rest period, the payroll designee pays the premium pay required by law and records it.

SB 525 health care minimum wage rates apply only to RCFEs affiliated with or controlled by an acute-care hospital or its parent. [AGENCY NAME] confirms annually, and documents, whether it is affected. If it is, the licensee obtains counsel's guidance on the applicable rates.
The licensee reviews exempt salary thresholds and minimum wage rates each January, adjusts pay by the effective date, and records the review.
The administrator keeps time records, pay records and sick leave records for the period required by California law, and makes them available to the employee on request.

Employees who believe they were underpaid or denied sick leave or breaks report it to the administrator or licensee. The licensee investigates within 10 days, corrects any underpayment promptly, and does not retaliate.

responsibilities.duty: Sets compliant pay and scheduling, classifies positions, and obtains employment counsel advice for live-in and 24-hour shifts.
Schedules shifts and breaks, approves time records and ensures resident coverage during breaks.
Calculates wages, overtime and sick leave, and keeps payroll records.
Record time accurately, take scheduled breaks and report any pay or break problems.

documentation: Offer letters and written notice of pay rate and sick leave
Exempt/non-exempt classification records
Time records and payroll registers
Paid sick leave accrual and use records
Break schedules and premium pay records
Written advice from employment counsel for live-in and 24-hour shifts
Annual minimum wage and SB 525 applicability review

policies.title: Resident Records, Register of Residents and Retention
policies.applies_to: Administrator, designated record keepers, direct care staff and the person responsible for medication storage
federal: 45 CFR Part 164 (HIPAA Privacy Rule, only if [AGENCY NAME] is a covered entity)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete, accurate and secure record for every resident, keeps the register of residents current, and keeps the specific records that 22 CCR §87507 and §87465 require for the periods stated.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a record for each resident and a register of residents as Title 22 requires. The original signed admission agreement and all signed modifications are kept in the resident's file. When the appraisal shows a hearing or other disability, a completed LIC 9158 is also kept in the file. PRN physician orders and dose records are kept in the resident's file. Centrally stored medication records are kept at least 1 year, and medication destruction records are kept at least 3 years. No other retention period has been verified for this policy. Until [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms the required period in writing with CDSS Licensing or legal counsel, no resident record is destroyed. Records are kept confidential and available to authorized persons and to CDSS Licensing.

definitions.definition: The file kept for each resident containing the admission agreement, appraisal, service plan, medical information, orders, incident reports and other documents required by Title 22.
The facility's current list of residents required by Title 22, showing each resident's name, admission and departure dates and other required information.
The records kept for medications stored in the facility's locked central storage.
A record of medication destroyed by the administrator and one other non-resident adult.

procedures: On or before the day of admission, the administrator opens a record for the resident and enters the resident on the register of residents with the required information. The register is updated the same day for every admission, discharge, transfer, hospitalization or death.

The administrator places the resident's pre-admission appraisal, service plan, medical assessment, emergency contacts, and the name and contact information of the person responsible for the resident in the file as required by Title 22.

The administrator makes sure the admission agreement is signed and dated by the resident or the resident's representative and the licensee within 7 days of admission, gives a copy immediately, and files the original signed agreement in the resident's file.
Any signed modification of the agreement, including a 60-day rate change notice and the resident's acknowledgment, is filed with the original agreement in the same file.
When the appraisal shows a hearing or other disability, the administrator completes LIC 9158 and keeps it in the resident's file.

The administrator files every PRN physician order, which must be signed and dated and state the symptoms, exact dose, minimum hours between doses and maximum doses per 24 hours, along with the record of each PRN dose given or assisted, in the resident's file.
Staff who assist with self-administered medications record each assistance on the medication record at the time it occurs, and the administrator reviews the records weekly.
For medications kept in central storage, the staff member responsible keeps a record, and the administrator keeps that record for at least 1 year.
When medications are destroyed, the administrator and one other non-resident adult both sign the destruction record. The administrator keeps the destruction record for at least 3 years.

Staff keep resident records in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. Records are not left unattended and are shown only to those who need them to give care, to the resident or representative, and to authorized agencies including CDSS Licensing and the ombudsman as permitted by law.

If [AGENCY NAME] is a HIPAA covered entity, the administrator follows 45 CFR Part 164 and RR-07 for uses and disclosures. If it is not, the administrator still applies the confidentiality protections in RR-07.
The administrator reviews each resident's record at least quarterly for completeness and corrects missing or outdated items within 7 days.

When a resident leaves, the administrator completes the register entry, adds the discharge or death information and keeps the record in a secure location. The record is not destroyed. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms in writing the required Title 22 retention period with CDSS Licensing or legal counsel before any destruction, and records the confirmation in the policy file.

The administrator makes the register and resident records available to CDSS Licensing on request during inspections and gives residents or their representatives access to their own records as the law allows.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the resident records and register, confirms retention periods before any destruction, and controls access.
Document medication assistance and care accurately and at the time they occur, and protect confidentiality.
Provides secure storage and supports confirming retention requirements.

documentation: Resident record and register of residents
Original signed admission agreement and signed modifications
LIC 9158, where required
PRN physician orders and dose records
Central medication storage records (kept at least 1 year)
Medication destruction records (kept at least 3 years)
Written confirmation of retention period before any record destruction
Quarterly record review checklist

policies.title: Required Reports and Notices to the State
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, designated substitute and all staff who observe or learn of a reportable event
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] makes every required report and notice to CDSS Community Care Licensing, the ombudsman, the local health officer, fire authority, law enforcement, residents and others on time, and pays the annual license fee when due.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] reports events and notifies agencies within the time limits in 22 CCR §87211. Written reports are made within 7 days for any death, any serious injury as determined by the physician, any AED use, and any incident threatening the welfare, safety or health of residents, including unexplained absence and psychological abuse. Outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes and major accidents are reported within 24 hours by phone or fax. Fires and explosions are reported immediately to the local fire authority and no later than the next working day to licensing. Suspected physical abuse of an elder or dependent adult is reported within 2 hours if there is serious bodily injury and within 24 hours otherwise. Staff are mandated reporters under Welfare and Institutions Code §15630. Financial distress events are reported within 2 business days. Administrator and chief corporate officer changes are reported within the deadlines below. The annual license fee is paid each year by the license anniversary. If a report time is unclear, the facility reports promptly and does not wait.

definitions.definition: CDSS Community Care Licensing Division, Adult and Senior Care Program, through the facility's regional office. Main phone: (916) 657-2592.
A care custodian or facility staff member who must report suspected elder or dependent adult abuse under W&I Code §15630.
The written report form for suspected elder or dependent adult abuse, sent after the phone report.
An injury involving extreme physical pain, substantial risk of death or protracted loss or impairment of function, which triggers the 2-hour abuse reporting time.
The resident's family member, representative or other person listed in the resident record as responsible.

procedures: Any staff member who sees or learns of a death, serious injury, AED use, threat to welfare, safety or health, fire, outbreak, poisoning, catastrophe, major accident or suspected abuse immediately gives first aid or calls 9-1-1 if there is an imminent threat, and then tells the administrator or designated substitute without delay.

For any death, any serious injury as determined by the physician, any AED use, or any incident threatening the welfare, safety or health of a resident (including unexplained absence and psychological abuse), the administrator submits a written report to the licensing agency and to the person responsible for the resident within 7 days of the event.

For an outbreak, poisoning, catastrophe or major accident, the administrator reports by phone or fax to the licensing agency and the local health officer within 24 hours, and follows with a written report within 7 days where the event also meets the 7-day criteria.
For a fire or explosion, the administrator or senior staff on duty reports immediately to the local fire authority and no later than the next working day to the licensing agency.

For suspected physical abuse of a resident, the staff member who suspects abuse makes a phone report immediately or as soon as practicably possible. The report goes to the local ombudsman, the licensing agency and local law enforcement. It is made within 2 hours if there is serious bodily injury and within 24 hours if there is not.

The reporter, or the administrator on the reporter's behalf, sends the written SOC 341 within the time set by statute. Each mandated reporter may report on their own. The administrator never blocks, delays or discourages a staff member's report.

The administrator records the date, time, agency, person spoken to, report number and method for every phone report on the facility's report log, and keeps a copy of every written report and fax confirmation in the resident record and the administrative file.

The licensee gives written notice within 2 business days to CDSS, the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman, residents and their representatives of any foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default notice or utility shut-off notice. The licensee also gives this notice to applicants before they sign the admission agreement.
The licensee understands that failure to give the financial notices can lead to a civil penalty of $100 per day, up to $2,000. The licensee keeps copies of each notice and proof of delivery.

When a new administrator is hired, the licensee notifies the licensing agency within 30 days. The licensee confirms the new administrator's certification (see GOV-02) and clearance (see STF-02) are on file before the administrator starts.
When the chief corporate officer changes, the licensee notifies the licensing agency within 15 working days.

The licensee pays the annual license fee by each license anniversary: $495.60 for facilities with 4 to 6 beds and $742.80 for facilities with 7 to 15 beds. A 50% late fee applies if the fee is late. A $25 capacity change fee applies when licensed capacity changes. The administrator puts the due date on the compliance calendar 60 days ahead.
The administrator reviews the report log at least monthly to confirm every event has the required reports and follow-up, and presents any gaps to the licensee within 3 days.
